name: ReconstructLargeScanToFile
label: Reconstruct Large Scan to File (Cone-Beam FDK)
description:
Cone-beam FDK reconstruction of a scan on disk straight into a file, for scans and volumes larger than memory. Projections are read a band of detector rows at a time and the volume is written a slab of slices at a time, with reading, filtering, GPU backprojection and writing running at once; memory use follows the Working Memory setting, not the size of the data. The result is the same as Cone-Beam FDK in memory.

Use it when the scan does not fit in memory, or the volume would not: 2048^3 voxels are 34 GB. For scans that need corrections Tomviz only does in memory (ring removal, alignment), correct them first and save the projections.

parameters.name: scan_file
parameters.label: Scan
parameters.description: A scanner project (Nikon .xtekct, Waygate .pca, Bruker SkyScan .log), a multi-page TIFF or one TIFF of a folder of projections, an HDF5 file (NXtomo or Data Exchange, with their flat and dark fields), or a .npy stack. Nothing is loaded into memory: detector rows are read as they are needed, so keep the scan on a fast drive (an NVMe drive is far faster than a hard disk here).

parameters.name: whole_folder
parameters.label: Every TIFF File in the Scan's Folder
parameters.description: For projections stored one TIFF file each: reconstruct every TIFF file in the chosen file's folder, in name order.

parameters.name: output_file
parameters.label: Write the Volume To
parameters.description: The reconstructed volume is written here as it is computed (EMD, the HDF5 layout Tomviz opens). Tomviz then shows a subsampled view of it; open the file for full resolution.

parameters.name: intensity
parameters.label: Projections Are
parameters.description: How intensities become line integrals, band by band as they are read. Auto uses the scan's flat and dark fields when the file has them, the scanner's open-beam level when it stores one, leaves floating-point data as it is, and otherwise estimates an open-beam level per projection from its brightest pixels.

parameters.name: i0
parameters.label: Open-Beam Level (0 = from the file or estimated)

parameters.name: geometry_source
parameters.label: Geometry
parameters.description: Scanner projects (Nikon .xtekct, Waygate .pca, Bruker SkyScan .log) carry their geometry; plain image stacks and HDF5 files do not, so the circular orbit below is used for them.

parameters.name: sod
parameters.label: Source to Rotation Axis Distance
parameters.description: Distance from the X-ray source to the rotation axis (SOD), in mm or any length unit used consistently.

parameters.name: sdd
parameters.label: Source to Detector Distance
parameters.description: Distance from the X-ray source to the detector (SDD).

parameters.name: pixel_size
parameters.label: Detector Pixel Size
parameters.description: Detector pixel pitch (as binned), in the same unit as the distances.

parameters.name: offset_u
parameters.label: Horizontal Detector Offset (pixels)
parameters.description: Where the central ray, through the rotation axis and perpendicular to the detector, hits the detector, in pixels from the detector centre across the rotation axis (along y). Use it to correct an off-centre rotation axis.

parameters.name: offset_v
parameters.label: Vertical Detector Offset (pixels)
parameters.description: Where the central ray hits the detector, in pixels from the detector centre along the rotation axis (along x).

parameters.name: clockwise
parameters.label: Reverse Rotation Direction
parameters.description: Turn this on if the reconstruction comes out mirrored.

parameters.name: geometry_file
parameters.label: Geometry Vectors File
parameters.description: Text file with one row of 12 numbers per projection: source position, detector centre, detector u step (across the rotation axis) and v step (along it), as in ASTRA's cone_vec geometry.

parameters.name: arc
parameters.label: Scan Arc (degrees)
parameters.description: For files that store no projection angles: the projections are taken as evenly spaced over this arc, the last one a step short of it.

parameters.name: short_scan
parameters.label: Short-Scan Weights
parameters.description: Parker weights for scans shorter than 360 degrees. Auto uses them when the scan is shorter than a full circle.

parameters.name: volume_size_xy
parameters.label: Volume Size Across the Axis (voxels, 0 = automatic)
parameters.description: Voxels in y and z. 0 covers the field of view.

parameters.name: volume_size_axial
parameters.label: Volume Size Along the Axis (voxels, 0 = automatic)
parameters.description: Voxels in x. 0 covers the field of view.

parameters.name: voxel_size
parameters.label: Voxel Size (0 = automatic)
parameters.description: 0 uses the detector pixel size divided by the magnification.

parameters.name: backend
parameters.label: Compute On
parameters.description: Auto uses a GPU through WebGPU (any vendor) when available and falls back to the CPU.

parameters.name: memory_gb
parameters.label: Working Memory (GB, 0 = half of what is free)
parameters.description: Memory for detector rows and volume slabs. More memory means fewer, larger slabs and less overhead; the volume itself never has to fit.

parameters.name: preview_voxels
parameters.label: Preview Size (voxels per axis, at most)
parameters.description: The view Tomviz shows is the volume subsampled to about this many voxels along each axis.
